subject: Hosted API sudden p95/p99 surge impacting OliveTech — mitigation plan and bridge
messages:
From: Jamie Cooper <jamie.cooper@olivetech.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: OliveTech SRE <sre@olivetech.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Alert: sharp p95/p99 jump & errors since 08:40 PST — OliveTech traffic

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing a serious regression on the Redwood Hosted API for our production traffic starting ~08:40 PST. Key symptoms: p95 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.4s, p99s up to ~3.6s, overall error rate rose to 2.8% (previously ~0.1%), and effective throughput for our requests dropped ~18%. This started suddenly and is impacting user flows.

Attached is a small sample of request IDs (request-sample-ids.csv) and a quick screenshot of our observability window. We believe this coincides with a larger spike in queue depth on your side — requests are piling and we're seeing timeouts.

Please escalate — this is affecting several customers. We need:
- a short RCA or at least a mitigation plan within the hour
- confirmation if you can route us to a different pool or reduce batching aggressiveness for our traffic
- any immediate workarounds we can implement client-side while you stabilize

Happy to join a bridge.

Thanks,
Jamie Cooper
Sr. Product Ops, OliveTech
jamie.cooper@olivetech.com

Attachment: request-sample-ids.csv (3KB)

I'll loop in ops and leadership in the next update.

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Alert: sharp p95/p99 jump & errors since 08:40 PST — OliveTech traffic

Thanks @Jasmine — quick triage notes from Engineering (summary):

What we see: 
- Queue depth for the hosted inference fleet serving that model spiked from a median of ~12 to ~120 concurrent queued requests between 08:35–09:10 PST.
- p95 increased from ~220ms to ~1.4s; p99 to ~3.6s; error rate increased to 2.8% (timeouts and 5xx from overloaded workers).
- Throughput dropped ~18% due to head-of-line blocking from large batches.

Likely cause: a rolling config change at ~03:00 UTC (05:00 PST) increased the default batch_wait_ms for that model family from 20ms -> 80ms and widened the batching window. For steady small-request workloads (like OliveTech), that change produced larger batch assemblies which lengthened per-request latency under load and caused queue formation. The change originally targeted throughput gains for larger enterprise jobs, but we didn't pin it per-customer.

Immediate corrective actions we recommend (can execute in the next 10–30m):
1) Roll back batch_wait_ms to 20ms for the OliveTech-serving config (target: 15m). Owner: grace_oconnor.
2) Temporarily route OliveTech to dedicated pool dedicated-olivetech-1 with 2x baseline capacity (target: 25m). Requires RB approval for credits. Owner: jasmine_liu + rachel_kim.
3) Raise max_concurrency_per_worker to reduce head-of-line blocking for short requests (target: 30m). Owner: tessa_morgan.
4) Add a short-lived per-customer override to limit batch_size to 8 for OliveTech (target: 20m). Owner: grace_oconnor.

I'll attach the p95 dashboard screenshot and a short log extract (olive_p95_screenshot_20280522.png).

We can push the rollback and per-customer overrides immediately and keep a watch for 1 hour. Recommend a paid capacity routing while we stabilize (credits to apply for 48h).

— Grace O'Connor
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: olive_p95_screenshot_20280522.png)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Jamie Cooper <jamie.cooper@olivetech.com>, OliveTech SRE <sre@olivetech.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API sudden p95/p99 surge impacting OliveTech — mitigation plan and bridge

Jamie — quick status update following the bridge and actions this afternoon: 

What we executed (timeline):
- 10:20 PST: rolled back batch_wait_ms from 80ms -> 20ms for OliveTech routing (Grace).
- 10:35 PST: applied per-customer batch_size cap = 8 (Grace).
- 10:50 PST: increased max_concurrency_per_worker by 30% for the serving pool (Tessa).
- 11:05 PST: routed OliveTech traffic to dedicated-olivetech-1 with a 2x temporary capacity bump (Jasmine/Rachel).

Immediate results: p95 dropped from peak ~1.4s to ~320ms within 20 minutes of the rollback; p99 reduced to ~750ms; error rate back under 0.3% and throughput returned to within 95% of baseline. We're continuing a tight 120-minute watch window.

Next steps / owners: 
- Grace: monitor for 24h and prepare short RCA on the config rollout that widened batch windows, include why per-customer overrides weren't applied earlier (ETA: 24h).
- Marcus: track credits usage (OLV-2028-07) and confirm billing/contract notes (ETA: EOD).
- Tessa: run a targeted load test mimicking OliveTech traffic pattern against the current config to validate stability before we relax overrides (ETA: 8h).
- Jasmine: schedule a follow-up with OliveTech leadership tomorrow to review RCA and remediation plan (ETA: 48h).

Attached is our mitigation playbook we used this afternoon (mitigation-playbook-v1.pdf). We'll keep the dedicated routing for up to 72h and step down incrementally once metrics are stable.

Proposed bridge invite: 16:55 PT today to confirm next steps — I'll send calendar. Please let me know if you need additional logs or a signed acknowledgement for the temporary credit.

Thanks for your patience. We're treating this as a Sev2 and will produce the RCA and timeline for permanent fixes.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
(Attachment: mitigation-playbook-v1.pdf)
